uncited: - 3D texture dataset partitioned into axis-aligned sub-volume bounding boxes.
- Updated orthogonal opacity map (used for subsequent sub-volumes in the same frame).
**Orthogonal Opacity Map:** A 2D array of floating-point values.
Each pixel represents the minimum opacity of the corresponding region in the frame buffer.
Since the box is axis-aligned, projections are rectangles.
An adaptive system to adjust the number of opacity map updates ($k$) per frame based on performance history to balance rendering speed and occlusion detection overhead.
The system starts with an empirically determined $k$ (typically 9) and maintains a performance history window.
Every $n$-th frame (e.g., $n=10$), it polls the performance using the number in range $[k-hw, k+hw]$ that has not been updated for the longest.
A technique to save time by culling points that are occluded by opaque volume material in front of their footprint.
It requires front-to-back rendering to maintain an opacity image.
Mueller '00 method: After compositing, convolve the opacity image with a box filter sized to the projected footprint.
Lee '00 method: Keep points in an octree and maintain a visibility map as a quadtree.
Check the projection of an octree node against the corresponding level of the visibility map quadtree.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of sub-volumes and the cost of projecting and checking against the opacity map.
